payload.headline: Historical approval bypass reportedly caused full system wipe; current Clay safety boundary must be semantic/runtime authority, not model/prompt/tool-policy convention.
material_findings: PF-L0-SAFE-001: skip_approval=True bypassed high-risk checks and the repair commit reports a full system wipe.
PF-L0-SAFE-003: later hard-delete guardrail removed delete tooling and blocked equivalent primitives, a direct Safe-Effect precursor but not closure proof.
PF-L0-SAFE-005: Firejail absence could fail open to unsandboxed execution; current enforcement must fail closed.
PF-L0-SAFE-008: a separate Projects agent moved from project sandbox to full-system authority, demonstrating subsystem-level capability drift.
PF-L0-SAFE-009: model refusals were historically removed/bypassed in some paths, so refusal behavior cannot serve as the execution boundary.

requested_branch_actions.clay: Keep Safe-Effect Geometry permanent; prioritize authority non-amplification and recoverability tests with compromised model intent.
requested_branch_actions.claycode: Make parent-to-child effect closure and fail-closed broker semantics compiler/runtime acceptance properties.
requested_branch_actions.frank: Keep Needle/model intent outside execution authority; route mutations through deterministic capability/commit mediation.
requested_branch_actions.harness: Add historical wipe reproduction, approval-token confusion, sandbox-loss, alternate-language destructive equivalents and capability-drift regressions.
requested_branch_actions.unifieddb: Treat protected-state mutation/recovery receipts and capability grants as exact transactional state, not prompt context.
requested_branch_actions.claygraph: Preserve these negative results and ancestry so future retrieval cannot normalize them into generic safety prose.

payload.epistemic_boundary: This history supports prioritizing and testing Safe-Effect invariants; it does not prove the proposed Clay effect algebra is sound or complete.
